audits.title: 854 An Audit of Perioperative Diabetes Management Against GIRFT Standards
audits.standard: GIRFT guidance for perioperative diabetes management
audits.setting: University Hospital Southampton, tertiary centre; NCEPOD Category 3 surgical inpatients

cycle1.result: HbA1c and ketones checked in 53%; intra-operative CBG monitoring 59%, recovery 63%; appropriate long-acting insulin on VRI 45%; anaesthetic-to-ward handover 42%; hyperglycaemia 42%, hypoglycaemia 21%.

audits.intervention: Planned before cycle 2: targeted education for surgical and anaesthetic teams and clearer handover processes.
audits.citation: Tan Y, Roa N, Trivedi D. 854 An Audit of Perioperative Diabetes Management Against GIRFT Standards. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.253.

audits.title: Management of patients with diabetes mellitus referred for elective surgery from primary care: the challenge of the 18 weeks pathway.
audits.standard: Glycaemic control optimisation before elective surgery (target not reported)
audits.setting: One primary care practice referring for elective surgery

cycle1.result: Only 46 had HbA1c measured preoperatively and only 8 had a practice nurse review to optimise control.

audits.citation: Kaczynski J, May J, Pogoda I, Caldwell G. Management of patients with diabetes mellitus referred for elective surgery from primary care: the challenge of the 18 weeks pathway. J Perioper Pract. 2010;20(11):411-413. doi:10.1177/175045891002001105. PMID: 21162358.

audits.title: Successful implementation of a perioperative glycemic control protocol in cardiac surgery: barrier analysis and intervention using lean six sigma.
audits.standard: Admission to CSICU with glucose <200 mg/dL (perioperative insulin protocol)
audits.setting: Cardiac surgical intensive care unit, Massachusetts General Hospital (large academic hospital)

cycle1.result: Fewer than 10% of patients admitted to the CSICU with glucose <200 mg/dL.

audits.intervention: Perioperative insulin protocol implemented using Lean Six Sigma, with barrier analysis, provider education and extension to the intraoperative period.

cycle2.result: More than 90% of patients admitted with glucose <200 mg/dL.

audits.citation: Martinez EA, Chavez-Valdez R, Holt NF, Grogan KL, Khalifeh KW, Slater T, et al.. Successful implementation of a perioperative glycemic control protocol in cardiac surgery: barrier analysis and intervention using lean six sigma. Anesthesiol Res Pract. 2011;2011:565069. doi:10.1155/2011/565069. PMID: 22091218.

audits.title: Perioperative management of diabetes in elective patients: a region-wide audit.
audits.standard: National guidance on management of adults with diabetes undergoing surgery (2011)
audits.setting: Hospitals across the North Western Deanery (region-wide trainee audit)

cycle1.result: HbA1c recorded preoperatively in 71%; VRIII not used when indicated in 11%; only 8% received recommended substrate fluid; hourly intra-operative CBG in 56%; CBG in recovery in 73%.

audits.other_findings: Mean fasting time was 12:20 h; 9% with abnormal HbA1c were not known to the diabetes team; WHO checklist used in 95%.
audits.citation: Jackson MJ, Patvardhan C, Wallace F, Martin A, Yusuff H, Briggs G, et al.. Perioperative management of diabetes in elective patients: a region-wide audit. Br J Anaesth. 2016;116(4):501-506. doi:10.1093/bja/aev554. PMID: 26873177.

audits.title: Making surgical wards safer for patients with diabetes: reducing hypoglycaemia and insulin errors.
audits.standard: National perioperative diabetes guidelines; aim to reduce hypoglycaemia, insulin errors and harm events by 50%
audits.setting: Vascular surgery wards, Northern Vascular Centre, Newcastle Upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Poor glycaemic control in 90% of amputation patients; hypoglycaemia and insulin management errors in 75%; less than 15% had specialist diabetes input; 20% needed third-party help for hypoglycaemia.

audits.intervention: Education and guidelines (2015), diabetes in-reach service (2016) and whiteboard sugar cube alert system for poor glycaemic control (2017) over three PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Hypoglycaemia reduced by more than 50%, insulin management errors by 70% and patient harm events by 75%.

audits.other_findings: The whiteboard alert system had the greatest impact.
audits.citation: Singh A, Adams A, Dudley B, Davison E, Jones L, Wales L. Making surgical wards safer for patients with diabetes: reducing hypoglycaemia and insulin errors. BMJ Open Qual. 2018;7(3):e000312. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2017-000312. PMID: 30057957.

audits.title: Diabetes in day case general and vascular surgery: A multicentre regional audit.
audits.standard: National guidelines: all people with diabetes should have HbA1c within 6 months before surgery, below 69 mmol/mol if safe
audits.setting: Seven hospitals in the East of England; elective day case general and vascular surgery

cycle1.result: 86.7% (157/181) had HbA1c tested within 6 months; 8.9% (14/157) had HbA1c ≥ 69 mmol/mol and 85.7% (12/14) of these proceeded to surgery without optimisation.

audits.citation: Fletcher E, Askari A, Yang Y, Adegbola S, Al-Obudi Y, Bernstein D, et al.. Diabetes in day case general and vascular surgery: A multicentre regional audit. Int J Clin Pract. 2020;74(4):e13472. doi:10.1111/ijcp.13472. PMID: 31884722.

audits.title: Perioperative variable rate intravenous insulin infusion: a quality improvement project on a vascular surgery ward.
audits.standard: Established standards for perioperative VRIII prescribing
audits.setting: Vascular surgery ward, Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 'Refer to paper chart' safety check used in 33%; rescue medication prescribed in 0%

audits.intervention: VRIII prescribing checklist, education of junior doctors and ward staff, and electronic prescribing updates

cycle2.result: 'Refer to paper chart' used in 77% (p=0.046); rescue medication prescribed in 65%

audits.other_findings: Post-intervention period (n=18) showed 67% and 50%. Sustained improvement in adjustment of oral diabetes medicines and insulins; some VRIII use unnecessary in type 2 diabetes.
audits.citation: Aimar K, Orozov N, Spencer-Jones K, Burhan H, Butler N, Kassim S, et al.. Perioperative variable rate intravenous insulin infusion: a quality improvement project on a vascular surgery ward. BMJ Open Qual. 2023;12(1):e002048. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2022-002048. PMID: 36813469.

audits.title: Perioperative prevention of euglycaemic diabetic ketoacidosis in people living with type 2 diabetes established on sodium-glucose transport-2 inhibitors - a cross-site multi-cycle audit.
audits.standard: Perioperative guidelines on preoperative cessation and postoperative re-initiation of SGLT2 inhibitors
audits.setting: Cross-site audit, surgical patients with type 2 diabetes (Chelsea & Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: Two cases of euglycaemic DKA identified (compliance figures not reported in abstract).

audits.intervention: Staff education and dissemination of guidance.

cycle2.result: Documentation and perioperative SGLT2 inhibitor cessation improved significantly; one further case of euglycaemic DKA.

audits.other_findings: Postoperative ketone monitoring remained suboptimal; capillary blood ketone monitoring has since been introduced in clinical areas.
audits.citation: Romain KA, Cheng J, Kim SHL, Watters K, Theodoraki A. Perioperative prevention of euglycaemic diabetic ketoacidosis in people living with type 2 diabetes established on sodium-glucose transport-2 inhibitors - a cross-site multi-cycle audit. Clin Med (Lond). 2025;25(5):100502. doi:10.1016/j.clinme.2025.100502. PMID: 40812666.

audits.title: Fewer cancellations, better care: Supporting patients with diabetes through surgery.
audits.standard: Local perioperative guideline for elective surgery in people with diabetes
audits.setting: Inner-city teaching hospital (Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust), London

cycle1.result: 10% of cancellations due to suboptimal diabetes control, 63% of these within 2 weeks of surgery; only 32% proceeded to surgery within 1 year of cancellation.

audits.intervention: New perioperative guideline for elective surgery in people with diabetes

cycle2.result: 7% of cancellations due to suboptimal diabetes control, none within 2 weeks of surgery.

audits.citation: Cope PJ, Highfield F, Camfield E, Taylor C, Saqib A. Fewer cancellations, better care: Supporting patients with diabetes through surgery. J Perioper Pract. 2026;36(7-8):442-448. doi:10.1177/17504589261427976. PMID: 41983575.
